Platts gives Hindustani wujūd body/person, an Arabic-origin loan. The SSNP Hindko/Gujari transcription uses y for its affricate j, as independently checked against the source, so survey vayūd corresponds to vajūd. The existing Hindi/Urdu donor is a provisional regional contact-language proxy; Punjabi mediation is possible and the edge does not skip to Arabic.

Platts identifies Hindustani piyāz onion as Persian, and Jambu already attests the regional Hindi pyāj donor. Survey pyāj/pyāz and vocalic or affricated variants fit this widespread loan family. Hindi/Urdu is used as a provisional contact-language proxy rather than claiming direct Persian transmission; Bengali/Oriya or neighbouring Pahari mediation may intervene, and final i is retained as regional adaptation.
